summary: FH official data: Swiss watch exports rose 9.1% in October 2026 to CHF 2,456.4 million, the fifth consecutive month of growth. Jan-Oct exports were close to CHF 22 billion (+3.4%). Growth was led by steel (+11.2%) and gold-steel (+28.3%) watches; precious metal was flat (+0.4%). The US rose 60.8% on a tariff-linked base effect; China fell 12.1%. FH cautions that gold prices, the strong franc and US tariffs weigh on margins, so export growth is not a full measure of the sector's health.

claims.text: Swiss watch exports grew 9.1% in October 2026 to CHF 2,456.4 million, the fifth consecutive month of growth.
claims.evidence: FH: 'Swiss watch exports grew by 9.1% in October, marking a fifth consecutive month of steady growth.' Table total CHF 2,456.4m, +9.1%.
claims.attribution: Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry FH

claims.text: Exports for January-October 2026 were close to CHF 22 billion, up 3.4% on the same period of 2025.
claims.evidence: FH: 'The cumulative value of exports over the first 10 months of year was close to 22 billion francs, a 3.4% increase.'
claims.attribution: Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry FH

claims.text: Wristwatch exports were 1.5 million units (+12.9%) worth CHF 2,343.8 million (+9.5%); almost 177,000 more watches than a year earlier.
claims.evidence: FH table: wristwatches 1.5m units +12.9%, CHF 2,343.8m +9.5%; text: 'almost 177,000 more than a year earlier.'
claims.attribution: Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry FH

claims.text: By material, steel watch value rose 11.2% (CHF 778.0m), gold-steel 28.3% (CHF 437.9m), other metals 31.0%; precious metal watches were stable at +0.4% (CHF 859.2m).
claims.evidence: FH 'Wristwatches by materials' table and text.
claims.attribution: Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry FH

claims.text: By market: USA CHF 363.7m (+60.8%), France CHF 239.8m (+101.6%), Hong Kong +7.3%, Japan -2.1%, China -12.1%, UK +6.5%.
claims.attribution: Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry FH

claims.text: FH says the US jump was driven by a favourable base effect linked to US tariffs; US exports Jan-Oct were down 0.1% vs 2025. France's +101.6% was mainly re-exports; the EU's +9.2% better reflects the regional trend.
claims.attribution: Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry FH

claims.text: All price segments grew: watches over CHF 3,000 export price +9.0% in value; under CHF 500 +23.5%; CHF 500-3,000 +6.6%.
claims.attribution: Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry FH

claims.text: FH cautions the figures should be read carefully: higher gold prices, a strong Swiss franc and US tariffs weigh on margins, so export growth is not a full measure of the sector's performance. Figures are exports, not retail sales.
claims.evidence: FH monthly analysis caveat paragraph and footnote.
claims.attribution: Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry FH

claims.text: FH's next release, covering November 2026, is scheduled for 17 December 2026.
claims.attribution: Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry FH
